title: Compatible injective columns for a ringed-topos Cech nerve
statement:
Let $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$ be topoi presented by small sites in fixed larger coefficient universes [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], with sheaves of commutative rings $R_X,R_Y$ and module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $f:(\mathcal X,R_X)\to(\mathcal Y,R_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] with Cartesian coefficient identification and exact module inverse image. Let $V\to1_{\mathcal X}$ be an epimorphism of sheaves of sets, $V_n=V^{\times(n+1)}$, and $v_n:\mathcal X/V_n\to\mathcal X$ the slice localizations with rings $v_n^*R_X$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. All diagrams are small. Use ordinary unbounded module derived categories with localization functor $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and finite-diagonal total complexes with differential $d_{\mathrm{Cech}}+(-1)^n d_I$ in Cech degree $n$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. For every $R_X$-module $K$ there exists an injective resolution $a:K[0]\to I^\bullet$ with $I^q=0$ for $q<0$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. The canonical element-site localization functors admit a coherent Cech image model [def-sfb-element-site-localization, def-sfb-coherent-cech-image-model]. For every such resolution and canonical model, $I$ and all $v_n^*I$ are K-injective [def-pur-kinjective-complex], and $v_n^*a$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The objects
$$B_V(I)^{n,q}=(fv_n)_*v_n^*I^q\quad(n,q\geq0)$$
with the actual face and degeneracy restrictions form a cosimplicial complex, whose alternating differential commutes with $d_I$ and squares to zero. The localization units define a chain map $a_V:f_*I\to B_V(I)^{0,\bullet}$ killed by the first Cech differential and a chain augmentation $b_{V,I}:f_*I\to\operatorname{Tot}B_V(I)$ whose degree-$q$ component is $a_V^q$ followed by the $(0,q)$ inclusion. There are specified canonical derived-comparison isomorphisms
$$Q(f_*I)\cong Rf_*(K[0]),\qquad Q(B_V(I)^{n,\bullet})\cong R(fv_n)_*(v_n^*K[0]).$$
They are the comparisons at $a$ and $v_n^*a$ from the right-derived units. The actual restriction maps on this one resolution, with their strict simplicial identities, give a coherent resolution model for the cosimplicial derived direct images and their augmentation.

proof.text: Apply the Grothendieck theorem for module sheaves to the chosen small presentation of $\mathcal X$, in the common larger universe containing its site and coefficients. Its module category has enough injectives. Clause (1) of the injective-resolution existence statement therefore gives $a:K[0]\to I$ with injective terms and $I^q=0$ for $q<0$. This is existence of an ordinary nonnegative resolution; the rest of the argument works for every such $a$.

source.place: Tag 013K, lemma-injective-resolutions-exist (1); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A5, section-unbounded, first paragraph

proof.text: The canonical element-module extension is left adjoint to canonical element-site restriction. The presheaf extension theorem proves that its presheaf pullback preserves finite limits; forgetting module sheaves and sheafification also preserve finite limits. The canonical pullback comparison therefore proves that elementModuleExtension preserves finite limits. The right-adjoint injectivity lemma makes elementModulePullback preserve injectives. Restriction is also left adjoint to the localization direct image, hence exact, and preserves the resolution quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text: The bounded-below injective-complex theorem applies both to $I$ and to every $j_{V_n}^*I$, since Step 2 gives injective terms and the same bound $0$. Hence these complexes are K-injective, with exactly the definition of K-injectivity used here. This does not require preservation of K-injectivity by a general exact inverse image; the exact extension-by-zero adjoint of the slice was essential in Step 2.

source.place: Tag 08FI, lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open, and its exact-left-adjoint argument; derived.tex lemma-acyclic-is-zero

proof.text: Choose the direct images $j_{A*}$ of the canonical element-site localizations. Their module adjunctions can be obtained from continuous-cocontinuous ringed restriction: the projection $(U,s)\mapsto U$ is continuous because covers on the element site are induced covers, and cocontinuous because a cover of $U$ lifts at $(U,s)$ by restricting $s$ to every member. Thus the cited theorem supplies the additive right adjoints with identity coefficient maps. For $b:B\to A$, the element functor $p_b:(U,t)\mapsto(U,b(t))$ satisfies $p_Ap_b=p_B$; it is continuous, since a family covers in $J_B$ or $J_A$ exactly when its image in $\mathcal C$ covers, and it has the same cover-lifting property. So $j_b^*$ of the element-site definition is defined. Relocalization identifies $j_b^*j_A^*$ with $j_B^*$ sectionwise. Set $E_A=j_{A*}j_A^*$. Define $r_b:E_A M\to E_B M$ to be the $j_B^*\dashv j_{B*}$ transpose of $j_b^*(\epsilon_A):j_b^*j_A^*j_{A*}j_A^*M\to j_b^*j_A^*M$, where $\epsilon_A$ is the counit at $j_A^*M$.

source.place: Tags 04IE and 04J4; sites.tex Tag 00XO; canonical adjunction construction on the element sites

proof.text: These arrows obey $r_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$ and $r_c r_b=r_{bc}$ for $c:C\to B$. Indeed their adjoint transposes are obtained by successive restrictions of the same counit; naturality of the counit and $\epsilon\circ j^*\eta=\mathrm{id}$ cancel the intermediate unit-counit pair. Sectionwise this says that restriction along $(U,t)\mapsto(U,b(t))\mapsto(U,b(c(t)))$ equals restriction along $(U,t)\mapsto(U,(bc)(t))$; identity restriction is identity. The units $u_A:M\to E_A M$ satisfy $r_bu_A=u_B$: transposing the left side gives $j_b^*(\epsilon_A\circ j_A^*u_A)=\mathrm{id}_{j_B^*M}$, the transpose of $u_B$. Every arrow is natural and additive in $M$, since restriction and the adjunctions are additive. Applying these functors termwise to a complex is therefore additive, including the alternating coface functor. This constructs all the data of a coherent Cech image model. For any supplied canonical model the same transpose characterization gives these same arrows.

source.place: Tag 04J4, lemma-relocalize-ringed-topos; elementary counit naturality and triangle identities

proof.text: Apply $f_*$ to $E_{V_n}(I^q)$ and to the restrictions just constructed. The direct image of a composite can be represented by the composite direct image: both are right adjoint to the same composite inverse image, and the unique adjunction-compatible comparison identifies their restrictions and units. Thus the entries are precisely $(fv_n)_*v_n^*I^q$. The coordinate deletion and repetition maps of $V^{n+1}$ satisfy the simplicial identities, since both composites in each identity select the same coordinates. Contravariant functoriality of $E$ makes these the strict cosimplicial identities on this one chosen model. Naturality in $I^q$ gives $d_I r_b=r_b d_I$. For $d_C^n=\sum_{i=0}^{n+1}(-1)^i\delta_i$, every composite of two cofaces occurs twice in $d_C^{n+1}d_C^n$, with opposite signs, by $\delta_j\delta_i=\delta_i\delta_{j-1}$ for $i<j$; hence $d_C^2=0$. This provides the claimed cosimplicial complex and commuting horizontal and vertical differentials.

source.place: Tag 04J4, lemma-relocalize-ringed-topos; coordinate simplicial identities and additive cancellation

proof.text: Let $a_V^q=f_*(u_V(I^q))$. Naturality of $u_V$ with respect to $d_I^q$ proves that $a_V$ is a chain map. The two maps $V^2\to V$ give the same composite with $u_V$, namely $u_{V^2}$ by Step 5; therefore $(\delta_0-\delta_1)a_V=0$. In total degree $q$, put $b^q=\iota_{0,q}a_V^q$. The $(1,q)$ part of $d_{\mathrm{Tot}}b^q$ is zero by the preceding equality. Its $(0,q+1)$ part is $a_V^{q+1}f_*d_I^q$, since the vertical sign at $n=0$ is $+1$. These are all its components, proving $d_{\mathrm{Tot}}b=bd$. The total differential squares to zero: the cross terms on $B^{n,q}$ are $(-1)^{n+1}d_Id_C+(-1)^nd_Cd_I=0$. Degree $m$ has only the summands $0\leq n\leq m$, as stipulated in the total-complex definition.

source.place: Tag 03FC, lemma-injective-module-trivial-cech, restriction augmentation; elementary first-quadrant total differential calculation

proof.text: Use the source library Functor.rightDerivedFunctor for each additive direct-image functor. Grothendieck module categories have K-injective resolutions, so its defining right-derived unit is universal on the homotopy category and invertible at K-injective complexes. Transport that unit through the quotient factorization to a unit on complexes. Whiskering by the full essentially-surjective homotopy quotient is fully faithful, hence the quotient factorization is a left Kan extension; composition of left Kan extensions proves the required universal property on complexes. Define each comparison by the unit at the K-injective resolution followed by the inverse derived image of its quasi-isomorphism. These formulas immediately give the displayed normalizations.

source.place: Tag 07A5, section-unbounded; derived.tex Tags 070Y, lemma-K-injective-defined and 070K, lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies

proof.text: Retain the complexes $f_*I$, $B^{n,\bullet}$ and all the actual restrictions, together with the comparisons of Step 8, as the resolution model of the derived diagram. Explicitly, if $c_n:Q(B^{n,\bullet})\to R(fv_n)_*(v_n^*K[0])$ is the displayed comparison, the derived arrow associated to a restriction $r:B^{n,\bullet}\to B^{m,\bullet}$ is $c_m Q(r)c_n^{-1}$; the derived augmentation is $c_0Q(a_V)c_{-1}^{-1}$ with $c_{-1}$ the first comparison. Multiplying two such arrows cancels the adjacent $c_n^{-1}c_n$, so every simplicial and augmentation identity follows from the strict identity in Step 6. This construction records the strict complexes and maps themselves, which is the coherent resolution model asserted in the statement. It does not infer coherence from an unspecified diagram in a triangulated category.
